The documentary finding is found in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Koki|en}}, compiled around 738 and cited in the {{ill|8=ja|9=令集解|Ritsuryoshukai|en}} 『令集解』巻7（神祇令）仲冬条 上卯相嘗祭（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。, which stipulates that offerings for the Ainamesai ceremony should be entrusted to the deities. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} According to the {{ill|8=ja|9=新抄格勅符抄|Shinsho Kakuchokufusho (New Text of the|en}} 『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒。 Court), dated 806, a {{ill|Daidō|total|en}} of 37 households were assigned to the " {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|en}} " (God of Wisdom) in 766 : 9 households from {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, 7 households from {{ill|Tamba Province|en}}, 10 households from {{ill|Harima Province|en}}, and 11 households from {{ill|Mimasaka Province|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} The {{ill|8=ja|9=新撰姓氏録|Shinsen Shojiroku,|en}} Kawachi Province, Shinbei section, contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest" 『新撰姓氏録』河内国神別 恩智神主条。 - [{{NDLDC|1879557/95}} 『群書類従 第十六輯』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）95コマ参照。, but this Onchi clan is believed to have been a worshipping clan ("Shinto priest" is {{ill|8=ja|9=カバネ|a kabane|en}}, a term derived from a job title), and the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en}}, {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Shogo Keiun|en}} 2nd year ( 768 ) entry 『続日本紀』神護景雲2年（768年）11月壬申（2日）条。 also contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest Hiroto" who was a Mimasaka no Jō {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} 「恩智神主」『日本古代氏族事典 新装版』 {{ill|佐伯有清|en}}編、{{ill|雄山閣|en}}、2015年。 . Before being moved to its current location, it was said to have been enshrined in {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} (present-day {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|Otabisho|en}} ) in the west. However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|lt=The national history|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|lt=the Jōgan|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）9月8日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 envoys were sent to this shrine along with 44 other shrines to offer prayers for protection from wind and rain {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . The {{ill|Engishiki|Shinmei-cho|en}} ( {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=list of deities|en}} ) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。 compiled in 927, stipulates that in Takayasu County, Kawachi Province, there are two Onchi Shrines, Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods), Tsukimi-no-Ainame-sai (festival of the Gods), and Niiname-sai (festival of the Gods), which are to be ranked as Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods) and to receive offerings at the Imperial Court's {{Interlanguage link|Tsukinami-no-matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-matsuri|en:draft}} (festival {{ill|Myojin Taisha|of the Gods),|en}} {{Interlanguage link|Ainame festival|ja|相嘗祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ainame festival}} (festival of the Gods), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-sai|en}} (festival of the Gods {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2年（939年）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3年（963年）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5年（994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017年）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2年（1109年）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409年）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」
（大阪府指定史跡）}}|en]] Furthermore, until the Meiji period, our company was in charge of Sarugaku at {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} in Nara . Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. In addition, {{ill|8=ja|9=銅鐸|bronze bells|en}} are also known to have been excavated north of Onji Shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} * [http://www.onji.or.jp/ Onchi Shrine] - Official website * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai6sibu/yao-city/m13_01_yao_onji.html Onchi Shrine] - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association * [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=64 Onji Shrine] - Yao City Cultural Property Information System * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=30401 Two Shrines of Onchi Shrine (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)] - Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program "Compilation of Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials" '''Affiliated shrines''' * Kasuga Shrine - deity: {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno Koyane no Mikoto|en}} '''Sub-shrine'''{{Hidden begin}} 恩智神社で年間に行われる祭事の一覧[http://www.onji.or.jp/03.html 恩智神社 > 行事]（公式サイト）。。 * 月始祭（毎月1日） * 歳旦祭（{{ill|1月1日|en}}） * お粥占神事・おき上げ神事（{{ill|1月15日|en}}） * 節分神事（2月） * 春季大祭（{{ill|4月3日|en}}） * 稲荷社祭典（{{ill|5月2日|en}}） * 夏越大祓神事（{{ill|6月30日|en}}） * 夏季大祭（{{ill|8月1日|en}}） * 愛宕神社festival・蛭子社御霊慰霊祭（{{ill|9月24日|en}}） * 天王の森・八坂社祭典（{{ill|10月17日|en}}） * 交通安全祈願祭（{{ill|10月18日|en}}） * 祖霊社御魂祭（{{ill|10月22日|en}}） * 御供所神事（{{ill|11月24日|en}}） - 八尾市指定無形民俗文化財。 * '''秋季festival（卯辰祭）''' ** 宵宮（{{ill|11月25日|en}}） ** 本宮祭（{{ill|11月26日|en}}） * 立松神事（{{ill|12月24日|en}}） * 年越大祓神事（{{ill|12月31日|en}}） {{Hidden end}} == Cultural Assets == === Cultural property designated by Osaka Prefecture === * Historic sites ** Onji Ruins - Designated on December 13, {{ill|1995|en}} [https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/bunkazaihogo/bunkazai/hunai-siteiichiran.html 大阪府内指定文化財一覧表]（大阪府ホームページ）の八尾市ファイルより。 [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 . === Yao City designated cultural property === * Sub-shrines within the precincts ** Tenkawa Shrine - deity: Kasuganobe Daimyojin ** Six companies *** Amaterasu Shrine - deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|en}} *** Tamasuo Shrine - deity: Kushiakira Tama *** Hiruko Shrine - deity: {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}} *** Kumano Shrine - deity: {{Ill|Kumanokusubi|en|4=fr}} *** Ankan Shrine - deity: {{ill|Emperor Ankan|en}} *** Sumiyoshi Shrine - deity: {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Sumiyoshi Daimyojin|en}} ** Atago Shrine - deity: {{ill|Izanami|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto|en}} ** Miwa Shrine - deity: {{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Omononushi-no-Okami|en}} ** Inari Shrine - deity: {{ill|Inari Okami}} ** Funato Shrine - deity: Funato Okami ** Ancestral shrine * Sub-shrines outside the precincts (temporary shrines) ** Yasaka Shrine - deity: {{ill|Susanoo|en}} == history == [[File:Onji-jinja,_sandou.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|天川山神宮寺感応院}}]] '''location''' * 5-10 Onchi Nakamachi {{ill|Yao, Osaka|lt=, Yao City,|en}} {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en}} '''Traffic access''' * Train: {{ill|8=ja|9=近畿日本鉄道|Kintetsu|en}} {{ill|8=ja|9=近鉄大阪線|Osaka Line|en}} {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智駅|Onji Station|en}} (approximately 20 minutes on foot) '''neighborhood''' * Tenkawasan Jinguji Kannoin Temple *: Motojingu-ji Temple, the 12th temple {{ill|8=ja|9=河内西国霊場|of the Kawachi Saigoku Pilgrimage|en}} . The museum's collection includes a wooden {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|lt=standing eleven-faced Kannon|en|10=fr}} statue ( {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|lt=an important cultural property|en}} ), a colored silk statue of Acala, and a gilt bronze four-pronged statue (a prefectural designated tangible cultural property). * {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onji Castle|en}} == Gallery == File:Onji-jinja,_kofun.jpg|link=File:Onji-jinja,_kofun.jpg|Main hall (left) and the ancient tomb behind it (right back) File:Onji-shrine02.JPG|link=File:Onji-shrine02.JPG|Akaido (Seimei Water)

{{Shrine |name = Onji Shrine |image = [[File:Onji-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = [[Osaka Prefecture]] [[Yao City]] [[Onji Nakamachi]] 5-chome 10 |latitude degrees = 34|latitude minutes = 36|latitude seconds = 23.47 |longitude degrees = 135|longitude minutes = 38|longitude seconds = 19.07 |ISO = JP-27 |enshrined deity = Ōmiketsuhiko no Ōkami
Ōmiketsuhime no Ōkami |sacred object = |rank = [[Shikinaisha]] ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} 2 seats)
(Traditionally) [[Kawachi Province]] [[Second Shrine]]
Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927年|927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2年（939年）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3年（963年）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5年（994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017年）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2年（1109年）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409年）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」

Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. {{神社 |名称 = 恩智神社 |画像 = [[File:Onji-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[大阪府]][[八尾市]][[恩智中町]]5丁目10番地 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 36|緯度秒 = 23.47 |経度度 = 135|経度分 = 38|経度秒 = 19.07 |ISO = JP-27 |祭神 = 大御食津彦大神
大御食津姫大神 |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[名神大社|名神大]]2座）
（伝）[[河内国]][[一宮|二宮]]
旧[[府社]] |創建 = 不詳 |例祭 = [[11月26日]]（卯辰祭） |本殿 = 王子造2棟 |別名 = 元春日 |札所等 = |神事 = 御供所神事（[[11月24日]]） |ラベル位置 = left |地図 = Osaka city }} {{座標一覧}} '''恩智神社'''（おんじじんじゃ/おんぢじんじゃ/おんちじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[八尾市]][[恩智中町]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）で、[[河内国]][[一宮|二宮]]と伝わる。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[府社]]。[[神使]]は[[ウサギ|兎]]と[[龍]]とされる。 == 祭神 == 現在の祭神は次の2柱神社由緒書。[http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。。 * '''大御食津彦大神'''（おおみけつひこのおおかみ、大御食津彦命） * '''大御食津姫大神'''（おおみけつひめのおおかみ、大御食津姫命） [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]等における祭神の記載は2座。『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』・『[[日本三代実録]]』の記載から2座の内容は「大御食津彦命神（大御食津比古命神）」・「大御食津姫命神（大御食津比咩命神）」であることが知られる。「ミケツ」の字義から食物を司る神（穀神）とされる{{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。現在の神社側では大御食津彦命は[[天児屋命|天児屋根命]]の後裔、大御食津姫命は[[トヨウケビメ|豊受大神]]（[[伊勢神宮]][[豊受大神宮|外宮]]祭神）に同じとし、本殿2棟に各1柱が祀られる。ただし天児屋命後裔の[[御食津臣命]]（大御食津彦大神）の妻[[御食津比売命]]（大御食津姫大神）は、『諸系譜』第六冊では[[天津日子根命]]の後裔とされている。 また、本殿2棟の間には春日辺神を祀る末社の天川神社が鎮座するが、この春日辺神とは[[天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|天照大神高座神社]]（八尾市教興寺、春日戸神）と見られることから、同神社と恩智神社との間の関係が推測される{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。[[江戸時代]]までは[[住吉大社]]に渡御する神事があったことや、『[[住吉大社神代記]]』に記述が見えることなどから、[[住吉三神|住吉神]]との関係を指摘する説もある{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。 社伝では[[奈良時代]]の[[天平宝字]]年間（[[757年|757]]-[[765年]]）に[[藤原氏]]によって再建された際に、藤原氏の氏神である[[天児屋命|天児屋根命]]が分祀され、摂社として社が建立された。それが[[宝亀]]年間（[[770年|770]]-[[781年]]）に[[枚岡神社]]に、次いで[[春日大社]]に遷座したとして、当社を「元春日」と位置づけている。しかし考証上では、[[中世]]頃以降に春日社家の大東家が恩智社家になったことで生じた伝承になるとされる{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 創建は不詳{{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}}。社伝（「恩智大明神縁起」）では、[[神功皇后]]の[[三韓征伐]]の際に[[住吉三神|住吉神]]・恩智神が現れて皇后を守護したので、恩智神は高安の七郷を賜ったとする{{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。また現在の神社側では[[雄略天皇]]14年頃の創建としている。 現鎮座地に遷座するまでは西方の[[天王の杜]]（現在の[[御旅所]]）に鎮座したというが、同地は[[弥生時代]]中期を中心とする遺跡（恩智遺跡）として知られ、恩智神社の創祀との関連性が指摘される{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。現社地への遷座の時期は確かではないが、伝承上では後述のように[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]初期頃という{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。 === 概史 === ==== 古代 ====

文献上の所見は『[[令集解]]』『令集解』巻7（神祇令）仲冬条 上卯相嘗祭（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。所引の[[天平]]10年（[[738年]]）頃成立の『古記』で、相嘗祭の班幣に預かる旨が規定されている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 『[[新抄格勅符抄]]』[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）牒『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒。では、[[天平神護]]2年（[[766年]]）に当時の「恩智神」に[[神戸 (民戸)|神戸]]として[[河内国]]から9戸・[[丹波国]]から7戸・[[播磨国]]から10戸・[[美作国]]から11戸の計37戸が充てられている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。『[[新撰姓氏録]]』河内国神別『新撰姓氏録』河内国神別 恩智神主条。 - [{{NDLDC|1879557/95}} 『群書類従 第十六輯』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）95コマ参照。では「恩智神主」の記載が見えるが、この恩智氏が奉斎氏族であったとされ（「神主」は職名が転化した[[カバネ]]）、『[[続日本紀]]』[[神護景雲]]2年（[[768年]]）条『続日本紀』神護景雲2年（768年）11月壬申（2日）条。にも美作掾の「恩智神主広人」が見える{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}「恩智神主」『日本古代氏族事典 新装版』 [[佐伯有清]]編、[[雄山閣]]、2015年。。 [[六国史|国史]]では、「恩智大御食津彦命神（恩智大御食津比古命神）」・「恩智大御食津姫命神（恩智大御食津比咩命神）」の[[神階]]が[[嘉祥]]3年（[[850年]]）に正三位、[[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）に従二位勲六等に昇叙された旨が記載されている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。また[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]元年（[[859年]]）『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）9月8日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。には他の44社とともに風雨を祈るための遣使奉幣がなされている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。では、河内国[[高安郡]]に「恩智神社二座 名神大 月次相嘗新嘗」として、2座が[[名神大社]]に列するとともに朝廷の[[月次祭]]・[[相嘗祭]]・[[新嘗祭]]では幣帛に預かる旨が定められている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。また『延喜式』臨時祭のうち、祈雨神祭条『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。では祈雨神祭八十五座のうちに恩智社二座と見えるほか、名神祭条『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。では名神祭二百八十五座のうちに恩智神社二座と見える{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。また『延喜式』四時祭下『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。では恩智社二座の祭料が規定されている{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 『[[本朝世紀]]』・『[[日本紀略]]』によれば、その後も[[天慶]]2年（[[939年]]）『本朝世紀』天慶2年（939年）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。・[[応和]]3年（[[963年]]）『日本紀略』応和3年（963年）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。・[[正暦]]5年（[[994年]]）『本朝世紀』正暦5年（994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。に風雨・疫癘のため奉幣が行われた{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。また[[寛仁]]元年（[[1017年]]）『左経記』寛仁元年（1017年）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。には天皇即位の大奉幣に際して河内国からは枚岡社（[[枚岡神社]]）と当社が選ばれ、[[天仁]]2年（[[1109年]]）『殿暦』天仁2年（1109年）10月29日条。には一代一度の大神宝使が河内国の中では当社のみに発遣された{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。[[永万]]元年（[[1165年]]）6月日の「神祗官諸社年貢注文」では、枚岡社・弓削社と並び「恩智社{{sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}}」と記載されている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 ==== 中世・近世 ==== [[中世]]期に入り、[[応永]]16年（[[1409年]]）『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409年）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。には御体御卜に祟る有力社に遣使があったうちに当社が見える{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。[[天文 (元号)|天文]]20年（[[1551年]]）の[[観心寺]]の正月会での諸神勧請の際は、河内国では枚岡大明神に続いて恩智大明神と見える{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 社伝（[[延宝]]3年（[[1675年]]）文書）では、[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]初期頃に[[楠木正成]]に従った[[恩智満一|恩智左近満一]]が[[恩智城]]を築城した際、城が神社を見下す形になったため旧社地（[[天王の杜]]）から現社地に遷座したというほか{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}、[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には[[織田信長]]の頃の放火で社殿が焼失したという{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 なお、一般に恩智神社は河内国で枚岡神社に次ぐ二宮の位置づけにあったといわれるが、中世期に恩智神社が二宮であることを示す確かな史料はない『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。。 ==== 近代以降 ==== [[明治維新]]後、[[1873年]]（[[明治]]6年）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列し、[[1912年]]（[[大正]]元年）に[[府社]]に昇格した{{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。 明治の[[神仏分離]]では[[神宮寺]]の天川山神宮寺[[感応院 (八尾市)|感応院]]が分離され、明治4年（[[1871年]]）に恩智神社境内の観音堂が感応院境内に移されている{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。 また、明治時代までは[[奈良]]の[[春日大社]]の[[猿楽]]は当社が受け持っていた。 === 神階 === * [[嘉祥]]3年（[[850年]]）[[10月7日]]、正三位（『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』）『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - 表記は「恩智大御食津彦命神」・「恩智大御食津姫命神」。 * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）[[1月27日]]、正三位勲六等から従二位勲六等（『[[日本三代実録]]』）『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - 表記は「恩智大御食津比古命神」・「恩智大御食津比咩命神」。 == 境内 == [[File:Onji-jinja, honden.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] [[File:Onji-jinja, tongu-2.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|頓宮の「天王の杜」
（大阪府指定史跡）}}]] 主要社殿のうち本殿は2棟からなり、いずれも王子造の切妻造である{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。造営年代は詳らかでないが、[[宝暦]]6年（[[1756年]]）頃と見られる{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。向かって右殿に大御食津彦命、左殿に大御食津姫命が祀られ、両殿の間に末社の天川神社が鎮座する。また両殿の周囲を玉垣・透塀で囲んだうえで各殿前に中門を設ける{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。両中門前には拝殿1棟（[[2000年]]（[[平成]]12年）再建）が建てられているほか、本殿の裏手には[[古墳]]1基があって[[横穴式石室]]を開口する{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。山麓の[[東高野街道]]沿いには[[鳥居]]が建てられている{{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}。 境内から西方約800メートル、現在の[[御旅所]]（頓宮）が所在する'''[[天王の杜]]'''（恩智中町3丁目、{{ウィキ座標|34|36|28.48|N|135|37|48.72|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|位置|name=旧鎮座地：天王の森（恩智遺跡）}}）は、恩智神社の旧鎮座地と伝える。現在は境外末社の八坂神社（牛頭天王社）が鎮座し、「天王」の呼称は同社に由来する{{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}}。同地一帯は[[縄文時代]]に始まる考古遺跡として知られ、特に[[弥生時代]]中期の集落遺跡が認められている。遺跡自体は南北1.2キロメートル・東西1.0キロメートルに広がるが、そのうち[[天王の杜]]を中心とする南北20メートル・東西50メートルが「恩智遺跡」として大阪府指定史跡に指定されている。なお関連して、恩智神社の北方では[[銅鐸]]の出土も知られる{{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}}。 File:Onji-jinja, kofun.jpg|本殿（左）裏手の古墳（右奥） File:Onji-shrine02.JPG|閼伽井戸（清明水）

Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927年|927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|lt=The national history|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2年（939年）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3年（963年）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5年（994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017年）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2年（1109年）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409年）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」

Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. {{Shrine |name = Onji Shrine |image = [[File:Onji-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = [[Osaka Prefecture]] [[Yao City]] [[Onji Nakamachi]] 5-chome 10 |latitude degrees = 34|latitude minutes = 36|latitude seconds = 23.47 |longitude degrees = 135|longitude minutes = 38|longitude seconds = 19.07 |ISO = JP-27 |enshrined deity = Ōmiketsuhiko no Ōkami
Ōmiketsuhime no Ōkami |sacred object = |rank = [[Shikinaisha]] ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} 2 seats)
(Traditionally) [[Kawachi Province]] [[Second Shrine]]
Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927年|927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 === Brief history === ==== Ancient ==== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:85%;background-color:#ffffff;white-space: nowrap;text-align:center;" !年 !{{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|枚岡神|en}} !恩智神 |- |836年 |従三位勲三等 →正三位勲三等 | |- |839年 |正三位勲三等 →従二位勲三等 | |- |850年 | |正三位 |- |856年 |従一位 | |- |859年 |従一位勲三等 →正一位勲三等 |正三位勲六等 →従二位勲六等 |- |860年 | | |- |{{ill|8=ja|9=延喜式神名帳|神名帳|en}} |名神大 |名神大 |- |{{ill|8=ja|9=一宮|一宮制|en}} |一宮 |（伝）二宮 |}
{| class="wikitable" style="font-size:85%;background-color:#ffffff;white-space: nowrap;text-align:center;" |+The {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine rank|en}} of the Main Gods of Kawachi ! Year ! Hiraoka God ! God of Wisdom |- | S.836 | Junior Third rank, Order of the Third Class




→ Third rank, Order of the Third Class | |- | S.839 | Third rank, Order of the Third Class




→ Junior Second rank, Order of the Third Class | |- | 850 | | Senior Third rank |- | S.856 | Junior First rank | |- | S.859 | Junior First rank, Order of the Sacred Treasure, Third Class




→ First rank, Order of the Sacred Treasure, Third Class | Third rank, Order of the 6th Class




→ Junior Second rank, Order of the Sacred Treasure, 6th Class |- | S.860 | | |- | {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Divine name List|en}} | Meishin University | Meishin University |- | {{ill|Ichinomiya|Ichinomiya System|en}} | Ichinomiya | (Translated by Ninomiya) |}
The documentary finding is found in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Koki|en}}, compiled around 738 and cited in the {{ill|8=ja|9=令集解|Ritsuryoshukai|en}} 『令集解』巻7（神祇令）仲冬条 上卯相嘗祭（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。, which stipulates that offerings for the Ainamesai ceremony should be entrusted to the deities. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} According to the {{ill|8=ja|9=新抄格勅符抄|Shinsho Kakuchokufusho (New Text of the|en}} 『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒。 Court), dated 806, a {{ill|Daidō|total|en}} of 37 households were assigned to the " {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|en}} " (God of Wisdom) in 766 : 9 households from {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, 7 households from {{ill|Tamba Province|en}}, 10 households from {{ill|Harima Province|en}}, and 11 households from {{ill|Mimasaka Province|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} The {{ill|8=ja|9=新撰姓氏録|Shinsen Shojiroku,|en}} Kawachi Province, Shinbei section, contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest" 『新撰姓氏録』河内国神別 恩智神主条。 - [{{NDLDC|1879557/95}} 『群書類従 第十六輯』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）95コマ参照。, but this Onchi clan is believed to have been a worshipping clan ("Shinto priest" is {{ill|8=ja|9=カバネ|a kabane|en}}, a term derived from a job title), and the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en}}, {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Shogo Keiun|en}} 2nd year ( 768 ) entry 『続日本紀』神護景雲2年（768年）11月壬申（2日）条。 also contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest Hiroto" who was a Mimasaka no Jō {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} 「恩智神主」『日本古代氏族事典 新装版』 {{ill|佐伯有清|en}}編、{{ill|雄山閣|en}}、2015年。 . Before being moved to its current location, it was said to have been enshrined in {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} (present-day {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|Otabisho|en}} ) in the west. However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|lt=The national history|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|lt=the Jōgan|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）9月8日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 envoys were sent to this shrine along with 44 other shrines to offer prayers for protection from wind and rain {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . The {{ill|Engishiki|Shinmei-cho|en}} ( {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=list of deities|en}} ) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。 compiled in 927, stipulates that in Takayasu County, Kawachi Province, there are two Onchi Shrines, Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods), Tsukimi-no-Ainame-sai (festival of the Gods), and Niiname-sai (festival of the Gods), which are to be ranked as Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods) and to receive offerings at the Imperial Court's {{Interlanguage link|Tsukinami-no-matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-matsuri|en:draft}} (festival {{ill|Myojin Taisha|of the Gods),|en}} {{Interlanguage link|Ainame festival|ja|相嘗祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ainame festival}} (festival of the Gods), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-sai|en}} (festival of the Gods {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2年（939年）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3年（963年）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5年（994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017年）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2年（1109年）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409年）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」
（大阪府指定史跡）}}|en]] Furthermore, until the Meiji period, our company was in charge of Sarugaku at {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} in Nara . Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927年|927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|lt=The national history|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|lt=the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} .
