Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category:Tier 2]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Onji Shrine]][[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: categories]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927th year |927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . The documentary finding is found in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Koki|en}}, compiled around 738 and cited in the {{ill|8=ja|9=令集解|Ritsuryoshukai|en}} 『令集解』巻7（神祇令）仲冬条 上卯相嘗祭（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。, which stipulates that offerings for the Ainamesai ceremony should be entrusted to the deities. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} According to the {{ill|8=ja|9=新抄格勅符抄|Shinsho Kakuchokufusho (New Text of the|en}} 『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒。 Court), dated 806, a {{ill|Daidō|total|en}} of 37 households were assigned to the " {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|en}} " (God of Wisdom) in 766 : 9 households from {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, 7 households from {{ill|Tamba Province|en}}, 10 households from {{ill|Harima Province|en}}, and 11 households from {{ill|Mimasaka Province|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} The {{ill|8=ja|9=新撰姓氏録|Shinsen Shojiroku,|en}} Kawachi Province, Shinbei section, contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest" 『新撰姓氏録』河内国神別 恩智神主条。 - [{{NDLDC|1879557/95}} 『群書類従 第十六輯』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）95コマ参照。, but this Onchi clan is believed to have been a worshipping clan ("Shinto priest" is {{ill|8=ja|9=カバネ|a kabane|en}}, a term derived from a job title), and the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en}}, {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Shogo Keiun|en}} 2nd year ( 768 ) entry 『続日本紀』神護景雲2nd year （768th year ）11月壬申（2日）条。 also contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest Hiroto" who was a Mimasaka no Jō {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} 「恩智神主」『日本古代氏族事典 新装版』 {{ill|佐伯有清|en}}編、{{ill|雄山閣|en}}、2015th year 。 . Before being moved to its current location, it was said to have been enshrined in {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} (present-day {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|Otabisho|en}} ) in the west. However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=The national history[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=the Kasho[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|lt=the Jōgan|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859年|859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）9月8日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 envoys were sent to this shrine along with 44 other shrines to offer prayers for protection from wind and rain {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . The {{ill|Engishiki|Shinmei-cho|en}} ( {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=list of deities|en}} ) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。 compiled in 927, stipulates that in Takayasu County, Kawachi Province, there are two Onchi Shrines, Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods), Tsukimi-no-Ainame-sai (festival of the Gods), and Niiname-sai (festival of the Gods), which are to be ranked as Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods) and to receive offerings at the Imperial Court's {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft}} (festival {{ill|Myojin Taisha|of the Gods),|en}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Ainame festival|ja|相嘗祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ainame festival}} (festival of the Gods), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-sai|en}} (festival of the Gods {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2nd year （939年）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3rd year （963rd year ）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5th year （994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017th year ）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2nd year （1109年）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409年）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」
（大阪府指定史跡）}}|en]] Furthermore, until the Meiji period, our company was in charge of Sarugaku at {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} in Nara . Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. In addition, {{ill|8=ja|9=銅鐸|bronze bells|en}} are also known to have been excavated north of Onji Shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} * [http://www.onji.or.jp/ Onchi Shrine] - Official website * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai6sibu/yao-city/m13_01_yao_onji.html Onchi Shrine] - It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927th year |927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=The national history[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=the Kasho[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859th year |859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2nd year （939th year ）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3rd year （963rd year ）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5th year （994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017th year ）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2nd year （1109th year ）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409th year ）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000年、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850年）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」
（大阪府指定史跡）}}|en]] Furthermore, until the Meiji period, our company was in charge of Sarugaku at {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} in Nara . Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. In addition, {{ill|8=ja|9=銅鐸|bronze bells|en}} are also known to have been excavated north of Onji Shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} * [http://www.onji.or.jp/ Onchi Shrine] - Official website * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai6sibu/yao-city/m13_01_yao_onji.html Onchi Shrine] - Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category:Tier 2]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Onji Shrine]][[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: categories]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927th year |927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=The national history[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=the Kasho[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859th year |859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2nd year （939th year ）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3rd year （963rd year ）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5th year （994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017th year ）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2nd year （1109th year ）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16年（1409th year ）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000th year 、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」

Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category:Tier 2]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Onji Shrine]][[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: categories]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927th year |927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} . The documentary finding is found in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Koki|en}}, compiled around 738 and cited in the {{ill|8=ja|9=令集解|Ritsuryoshukai|en}} 『令集解』巻7（神祇令）仲冬条 上卯相嘗祭（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。, which stipulates that offerings for the Ainamesai ceremony should be entrusted to the deities. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} According to the {{ill|8=ja|9=新抄格勅符抄|Shinsho Kakuchokufusho (New Text of the|en}} 『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806th year ）牒。 Court), dated 806, a {{ill|Daidō|total|en}} of 37 households were assigned to the " {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|en}} " (God of Wisdom) in 766 : 9 households from {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, 7 households from {{ill|Tamba Province|en}}, 10 households from {{ill|Harima Province|en}}, and 11 households from {{ill|Mimasaka Province|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} The {{ill|8=ja|9=新撰姓氏録|Shinsen Shojiroku,|en}} Kawachi Province, Shinbei section, contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest" 『新撰姓氏録』河内国神別 恩智神主条。 - [{{NDLDC|1879557/95}} 『群書類従 第十六輯』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）95コマ参照。, but this Onchi clan is believed to have been a worshipping clan ("Shinto priest" is {{ill|8=ja|9=カバネ|a kabane|en}}, a term derived from a job title), and the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en}}, {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Shogo Keiun|en}} 2nd year ( 768 ) entry 『続日本紀』神護景雲2nd year （768th year ）11月壬申（2日）条。 also contains a record of "Onchi Shinto priest Hiroto" who was a Mimasaka no Jō {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} 「恩智神主」『日本古代氏族事典 新装版』 {{ill|佐伯有清|en}}編、{{ill|雄山閣|en}}、2015th year 。 . Before being moved to its current location, it was said to have been enshrined in {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} (present-day {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|Otabisho|en}} ) in the west. However, the same place is known as an archaeological site (Onchi ruins) dating back to the middle of {{ill|Yayoi period|lt=the Yayoi period|en}}, and a connection to the founding of Onchi Shrine has been pointed out. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} It is unclear when the shrine was moved to its current location, but according to legend it was around the beginning of {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=the Nanboku-cho period|en}}, as will be described later. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} {{ill|Rikkokushi|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=The national history[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} records that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Divine ranks|en}} of "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto)" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto (Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto)" were elevated to Senior Third rank in the third year of {{ill|Kashō (early Heian period)|[[Category:nowiki former opening]]lt=the Kasho[[Category:nowiki former closing]]|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and to Junior Second rank, Sixth Class in the third year of the {{ill|Ten'an|en}} era ( {{ill|8=ja|9=859th year |859|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . The {{ill|Engishiki|Shinmei-cho|en}} ( {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=list of deities|en}} ) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。 compiled in 927, stipulates that in Takayasu County, Kawachi Province, there are two Onchi Shrines, Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods), Tsukimi-no-Ainame-sai (festival of the Gods), and Niiname-sai (festival of the Gods), which are to be ranked as Myojin Taisha (Great Shrines of Great Gods) and to receive offerings at the Imperial Court's {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft}} (festival {{ill|Myojin Taisha|of the Gods),|en}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Ainame festival|ja|相嘗祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ainame festival}} (festival of the Gods), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|lt=Niiname-sai|en}} (festival of the Gods {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In addition, among the temporary festivals in the Engishiki, the Rain-Praying festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）祈雨神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 85 rain-praying festivals, while the Meishin festival section 『延喜式』巻3（臨時祭）名神祭条。 lists two Onchi Shrines among the 285 Meishin festivals. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} Additionally, the Engishiki, Section 2 of the Four Seasonal festivals 『延喜式』巻2（四時祭下）十一月祭 恩智社二座条。, stipulates the offerings for the two Onchi Shrines. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} ==== Middle Ages and Early Modern Periods ==== According to {{ill|8=ja|9=本朝世紀|the Honcho Seiki|en}} and {{ill|8=ja|9=日本紀略|Nihon Kiryaku books|en}}, offerings were made to {{ill|Tengyō|the shrine|en}} in 939 (the second year of {{ill|Ōwa|Tenkei|en}} {{ill|939|era|en}} ) 『本朝世紀』天慶2nd year （939th year ）7月8日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/28}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）28コマ参照。, {{ill|963|lt=963 (the third year of|en}} Owa era) 『日本紀略』応和3rd year （963rd year ）7月15日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991095/459}} 『国史大系 第5巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）459コマ参照。, and {{ill|Shōryaku|994|en}} (the fifth {{ill|994|year of Shoreki|en}} 『本朝世紀』正暦5th year （994）4月27日条。 - [{{NDLDC|991098/112}} 『国史大系 第8巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）112-113コマ参照。 due to severe weather and epidemics. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, in the first year of {{ill|Kannin|lt=the Kannin|en}} era ( {{ill|1017|en}} ) 『左経記』寛仁元年（1017th year ）10月2日条。 - [{{NDLDC|1917934/29}} 『史料通覧 左経記』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）29-30コマ参照。, {{ill|8=ja|9=枚岡神社|Hiraoka Shrine|en}} and this shrine were selected from Kawachi Province to make a great offering to the emperor when he ascended to the throne, and in the second year of {{ill|Tennin (era)|lt=the Tennin|en}} era ( {{ill|1109|en}} ) 『殿暦』天仁2nd year （1109th year ）10月29日条。 the once-in-a-lifetime divine messenger was sent only to this shrine in Kawachi Province {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . In the "Order for annual Taxes from the {{ill|Eiman|Shrines|en}} " dated June {{ill|1165|en}}, the first year of the Eiman era, the shrine is listed alongside the Hiraoka Shrine and the Yuge Shrine as " {{Sub|鳥羽院女房右門子孫伝領云々}} Emperor Toba, Uemon." {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages, in {{ill|1409|en}} (the 16th year of the {{ill|Ōei|lt=Oei era|en}} ) 『続左丞抄』所収 応永16th year （1409th year ）12月10日神祇官解。 - [{{NDLDC|991102/737}} 『国史大系 第12巻』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）737-738コマ参照。, an envoy was sent to a powerful shrine that was suspected of causing hauntings, and this shrine was discovered there {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} . During the New Year's celebration at {{ill|Tenbun|lt=Kanshinji|en}} Temple in {{ill|1551|en}}, it appears that Onji Daimyojin was enshrined after Hiraoka Daimyojin in Kawachi Province. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} In addition, it is generally said that Onji Shrine was ranked second to Hiraoka Shrine in Kawachi Province, but there is no reliable historical evidence to show that Onji Shrine was the second shrine in the Middle Ages. 『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』 中世諸国一宮制研究会編、岩田書院、2000th year 、pp. 49-50。 ==== Modern and later ==== After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|lt=the Meiji Restoration|en}}, in {{ill|1873|en}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a village shrine|en}} under {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|the modern shrine ranking system|en}}, and in {{ill|1912|en}}, it was promoted to a prefectural {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|shrine|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} During the Meiji {{ill|8=ja|9=神仏分離|separation of Shinto|en}} and Buddhism, the shrine temple, {{ill|Kannō-in Temple (Yao City)|ja|感応院_(八尾市)|lt=Kannō-in Temple}}, was separated, and in {{ill|1871|en}} the Kannon Hall in the grounds of Onchi Shrine was moved to the grounds of Kan'on-in {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . According to the shrine's {{ill|Enpō|lt=history|en}} (document from [[1675]] ), when {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智満一|Onchi Sakon, who served under Kusunoki|en}} {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|lt=Masashige|en}} in the early {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|lt=Nanboku-cho|en}} period, built {{ill|8=ja|9=恩智城|Onchi Castle|en}}, the castle came to look down on the shrine, so the shrine was moved from its former location ( {{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}} ) to its current location {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . It is also said that during {{ill|Sengoku period|lt=the Sengoku period|en}}, the shrine building was burned down in an arson attack during the time of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en}} . {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} === God Tier === * {{ill|October 7|en}}, 850, third year {{ill|Kashō|lt=of the Kasho|en}} era ( {{ill|850|en}} ), awarded the rank of Shosanmi (Senior Third rank) ( {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|The Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} ) 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazutsuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazutsuhime no Mikoto". * On {{ill|Ten'an|lt=January|en}} {{ill|January 27|lt=27|en}}, 859, he was promoted from Senior Third rank, Sixth Class to Junior Second rank, {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Sixth Class (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en}} ) 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - written as "Onchi Omikazuhiko no Mikoto" and "Onchi Omikazuhime no Mikoto". == Temple grounds == [[File:Onji-jinja,_honden.jpg|right|thumb|250x250px|{{Center|main hall}}|en]] [[File:Onji-jinja,_tongu-2.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|頓宮の「天王の杜」
（大阪府指定史跡）}}|en]] Furthermore, until the Meiji period, our company was in charge of Sarugaku at {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} in Nara . Among the main shrine buildings, the main hall consists of two buildings, both of which are gabled in the Oji style. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The exact date of construction is unknown, but {{ill|1756|lt=it is believed to have been around 1756.|en}} {{ill|Hōreki|[|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} Facing the shrine, Omikazuchihiko is enshrined in the right hall, and Omikazuchihime is enshrined in the left hall, with the branch shrine of Tenkawa Shrine located between the two halls. In addition, both halls are surrounded by stone fences and lattice walls, and middle gates are set up in front of each hall. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} In front of both middle gates there is a worship hall (rebuilt {{ill|Heisei period|lt=in|en}} {{ill|2000|en}} [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 ), and behind the main hall there is an {{ill|Kofun|lt=ancient tomb|en}} with an open {{ill|8=ja|9=横穴式石室|horizontal stone chamber|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} . {{ill|Torii|lt=A torii gate|en}} has been erected along {{ill|8=ja|9=東高野街道|the Higashi-Koyasan Kaido road|en}} at the foot of the mountain. {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}}   == Sub-shrines == [[File:Onji-jinja,_Kasuga-jinja.jpg|right|thumb|220x220px|{{Center|春日神社}}]] There are 13 subsidiary shrines in total, including 1 subsidiary shrine (a shrine within the precincts) and 12 subsidiary shrines (11 within the precincts and 1 outside the precincts) [http://www.onji.or.jp/02.html 恩智神社 > 境内]（公式サイト）。 . About 800 meters west of the shrine grounds, '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Onchi Nakamachi 3-chome, 北緯34度36分28.48秒 東経135度37分48.72秒 ), where the current {{ill|8=ja|9=御旅所|shrine|en}} (tonmiya) is located, is said to be the former site of Onchi Shrine. Currently, the shrine is home to the Yasaka Shrine (Gozu Tenno Shrine), a branch shrine outside the precincts, and the name "Tenno" comes from this shrine. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The area is known for its archaeological sites dating back to {{ill|Jōmon period|lt=the Jomon period|en}}, and in particular the remains of a settlement dating back to the middle {{ill|Yayoi period|en}} . [http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=30 恩智遺跡]（八尾市文化財情報システム）。 The ruins themselves extend over an area of 1.2 kilometers from north to south and 1.0 kilometers from east to west, of which a 20-meter-wide area centered on '''{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori|ja|%E5%A4%A9%E7%8E%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%9D%9C}}''' (Tenno Forest) measuring 50 meters from east to west and known as the Onchi Ruins, has been designated as a historic site by Osaka Prefecture. Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] |established = Unknown |annual festival = [[November 26]] (Utatatsusai) |main hall = Ōji-style, 2 buildings |alternate name = Motokasuga |pilgrimage stamps = |rituals = Mikutosho Ritual ({{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}}) |label position = left |map = Osaka city }} [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Shrines in Osaka]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category:Tier 2]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Onji Shrine]][[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]][[Category: tier 3]][[Category: categories]] [[Category:Onji Shrine]][[ja:恩智神社]] '''Onji Shrine''' (恩智神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Onji Nakamachi, Yao, Osaka|ja|恩智中町}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|ja|八尾市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is an ancient shrine recorded as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}) and is traditionally considered the Ninomiya or second ranked shrine of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|府社}}. The shrine’s [[Shinshi|messengers]] are said to be rabbits and dragons. == Enshrined deities == The current enshrined deities are the following two 神社由緒書。 [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . * '''Omiketsuhiko-no-Okami''' (Omiketsuhiko the Wolf) * '''Omiketsuhime the Great Goddess''' (Omiketsuhime the Wolf) {{Small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} The {{ill|Engishiki|Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}} (list of Shinto deities) 『延喜式』巻9（神名上）河内国高安郡条。, compiled in the 5th year {{ill|Enchō|lt=of the Encho era|en}} ( {{ill|8=ja|9=927th year |927|en}} ), lists two enshrined deities. From the records in the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本文徳天皇実録|Chronicles of Emperor Montoku in Japan|en}} " 『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3rd year （850th year ）10月辛亥（7日）条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 and the " {{ill|8=ja|9=日本三代実録|Chronicles of the Three Generations of Japan|en}} " 『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859th year ）正月27日条（{{Harvard citation no brackets|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 it is known that the two shrines were "Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto (Omikazuchihiko no Mikoto)" and "Omikazuchihime no Mikoto (Omikazuchihime no Mikoto)." The literal meaning of "Miketsu" is that of a god of food (grain god) {{Sfn|恩智神社（国史）}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . At the present shrine, Omikazuchihiko-no-Mikoto is considered a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=天児屋命|Ameno-Koyane-no-Mikoto|en}}, and Omikazuchihime-no-Mikoto is considered to be the same as {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Toyouke-no-Okami|en}} (the deity enshrined {{ill|8=ja|9=豊受大神宮|at the Outer Shrine|en}} {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|of Ise Jingu|en}} ) 神社由緒書。, and one deity is enshrined in each of the two main buildings. However, in the sixth volume of "Shokeifu," {{ill|御食津臣命|Miketsuhime|en}} ( {{ill|御食津比売命|Omikazutsuhime), the wife of Miketsunoomi|en}} (Omikazutsuhiko-no-Okami), a descendant of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|8=ja|9=アマツヒコネ|Ame-no-Hikone-no-Mikoto|en}} . In addition, between the two main halls is the Tenkawa Shrine, a sub-shrine dedicated to Kasugano-kami, which is thought to be the same as {{ill|8=ja|9=天照大神高座神社・岩戸神社|Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine|en}} (Kasugado Shrine, Kyokoji Temple, Yao City), suggesting a relationship between this shrine and Onchi Shrine {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . Some theories point out a connection with the Sumiyoshi deity, based on the fact that there was a Shinto ritual in which the deity would be paraded around {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine|en}} until {{ill|Edo period|the Edo period|en}} and that a description of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the deity|en}} can be found in the {{ill|8=ja|9=住吉大社神代記|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|en}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（平凡社）|1986}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} . == External link == === founded === According to the shrine's legend, when it was rebuilt by {{ill|8=ja|9=藤原氏|the Fujiwara clan|en}} during the {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Tenpyo-Hoji|en}} era ( 757-765 ) of {{ill|Nara period|the Nara period|en}}, Ameno-Koyane- no -Mikoto, the clan deity of the Fujiwara clan, was enshrined there and a shrine was built as a sub-shrine. It was moved to Hiraoka Shrine and then to {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Taisha Shrine|en}} during {{ill|Hōki|the Hōki|en}} era ( 770-781 ), and the shrine is therefore positioned as the "Moto-Kasuga" [http://www.onji.or.jp/01.html 恩智神社 > 由緒]（公式サイト）。 . However, historical research suggests that this legend arose after {{ill|Middle Ages|the Middle|en}} Ages when the Daito family of the Kasuga Shrine became the Onchi Shrine family. {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（神々）|2000}} The date of its founding is unknown. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} According to the shrine's legend ("Onji Daimyojin Engi"), when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Empress Jingu|en}} was {{ill|8=ja|9=三韓征伐|conquering the Three Kingdoms of Korea|en}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|the Sumiyoshi deity|en}} Onji appeared and protected her, and so Onji was given the seven villages of Takayasu as a gift. {{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}} {{Sfn|恩智神社（式内社）|1979}} The current shrine claims that it was founded around the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku's reign|en}} .
